cf.title: Validate JSON object keys before omitting null values (BUG #19736)

input.subject: BUG #19736: `JSON_OBJECT ... ABSENT ON NULL` accepts invalid keys when the value is NULL

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection is fatal, and the goal of consistent key validation is clear. standards-compat-1 and standards-compat-2 are fixable points on back-patch scope, a release note and the SQL standard's rule for omitted pairs. A committer who knows SQL/JSON has to decide those, and none has spoken in the visible thread.

brief.title: Validate JSON object keys even when ABSENT ON NULL omits the pair
brief.problem: JSON_OBJECT with ABSENT ON NULL skips key validation when the value is NULL, so it returns {} for a NULL key or an array key. The same keys are rejected when the value is not NULL or when uniqueness is checked. The reporter reads the documented key restrictions as applying to omitted pairs too.
brief.proposed_design: The patch moves the json NULL-key check before the ABSENT ON NULL skip. Before an entry is skipped without a uniqueness check, it classifies the key type and rejects the same categories the conversion routines reject, without calling output or cast functions. v2 adds a shared helper json_validate_key_category(), applies the same fix to json_object_agg_strict() and jsonb_object_agg_strict(), and updates the documentation.
user_visible_surface: JSON_OBJECT ... ABSENT ON NULL now errors on NULL, array, composite, json and jsonb keys when the value is NULL.
JSON_OBJECTAGG ... ABSENT ON NULL gets the same key validation.
json_object_agg_strict() and jsonb_object_agg_strict() reject invalid keys paired with NULL values.
The documentation states that key restrictions apply even when the pair is omitted.
author_claims: The new regression tests fail without the fix, and all 239 core regression tests pass with it on macOS/arm64 with assertions.
Omitted keys still do not invoke output conversion without uniqueness checking, and WITH UNIQUE KEYS behaves as before.
jsonb keys were already covered in v1 because json_categorize_type() maps jsonb to JSONTYPE_JSON.
v3 is a rebase with no behavior changes from v2.
A second poster's 260-case test matrix found 19 invalid-key cases now rejected and no other result changes.
brief.thread_state: Dmitry Dolgov asked for a documentation change, a check of similar aggregate cases, a shared helper, and an explanation for JSONTYPE_JSONB; v2 and v3 address these. No one has replied to v2 or v3, and no committer has said whether the change should be back-patched.
unclear: The thread does not say whether this fix goes into stable branches, where queries that now return {} would start to fail.
No one discusses whether the SQL standard requires key validation for pairs that ABSENT ON NULL omits.
Dmitry Dolgov's point that skipping validation may be acceptable has no reply on the design choice itself.
The thread does not mention a release-note entry for the behavior change.

prior_attempts.title: COPY: validate option presence rather than option values
prior_attempts.quote: My concern is that the proposed patch could make the command unnecessarily less flexible.
prior_attempts.reason: Masahiko Sawada argued that "allowed only when" can be read as "allowed to be enabled only when", and that the patch makes COPY less flexible for tools that generate COPY commands with explicit true/false values. He added that VACUUM treats its boolean options the same way. The author withdrew the patch after Fujii-san raised the same objection on a related patch.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P11 rejected COPY options by their presence instead of their value. This patch rejects JSON keys whose pair is dropped anyway. Both add checks on input that does not affect the result.

prior_attempts.title: Revert cascading of JSON_TABLE's ON ERROR
prior_attempts.reason:
86ab7f4c721d commit made the table-level ON ERROR clause serve as the default
ON ERROR for columns lacking their own, so that a top-level ERROR ON ERROR
turned per-column evaluation errors into hard errors.

The SQL standard does mandate this cascade, but introducing it should be
a deliberate, separately-documented change, so restore the previous
behavior for now.  This also reverts the paired ruleutils.c logic that
deparsed a column's behavior against an ERROR default: that dropped an
explicit ERROR ON EMPTY from a dumped view, and otherwise emitted a
redundant NULL ON EMPTY.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P7 changed how ON ERROR cascades in JSON_TABLE, and this patch changes key validation in the SQL/JSON constructors. Both change SQL/JSON behavior that existing queries may rely on.

objections.title: Queries that return {} today start failing, with no back-patch or release-note plan
objections.failure_scenario: An application runs JSON_OBJECTAGG(k VALUE v ABSENT ON NULL RETURNING json) over a left join, so unmatched rows give a NULL key with a NULL value. Today the server skips such a row. After a minor or major upgrade the whole aggregate raises an error, and the user finds out in production.
objections.argument: The patch turns accepted inputs into errors for both constructors and aggregates (message #7), so users see a behavior change. Message #4 counts 19 previously accepted cases that are now rejected. No message says whether this goes to stable branches or gets a release-note entry. [P7] records that a change to SQL/JSON semantics should be deliberate and documented on its own.
objections.author_must_show: Is the fix meant for master only, and which release-note text tells users that ABSENT ON NULL now rejects NULL or non-scalar keys with NULL values?

precedents.title: Revert cascading of JSON_TABLE's ON ERROR

critic.reasoning: Message #4 counts 19 accepted cases that now fail, and no message settles back-patching or a release note. The scenario needs JSON_OBJECT or a non-scalar key, because the aggregates already reject NULL keys.

objections.title: The chosen semantics for omitted pairs are not checked against the SQL standard
objections.failure_scenario: The patch documents that key restrictions apply even to omitted pairs, which makes the behavior a promise. If the standard does not check a pair that ABSENT ON NULL drops, Postgres rejects queries that other conforming systems accept. Users who port SQL/JSON code then hit errors that only Postgres raises.
objections.argument: In message #6 Dmitry Dolgov says one can argue that skipped pairs need no key check, and that only the current doc wording insists on it. No reply addresses this design question. The patch then changes the documentation to match the code (message #7), so the wording settles the question instead of the standard. The array, composite and json key rules are Postgres-specific, but the NULL-key case may be covered by the standard's constructor rules.
objections.author_must_show: What does the SQL standard say about a NULL key whose pair ABSENT ON NULL drops, and does the patch follow it?

critic.reasoning: No message cites the SQL standard for a NULL key whose pair ABSENT ON NULL drops. Dmitry Dolgov's proposed wording in message #6 supports the stricter reading, but it does not answer the standard question.

refuted.title: Stricter key checks turn working queries into errors, back-patch scope unsettled
refuted.failure_scenario: An application runs jsonb_object_agg_strict(k, v), or JSON_OBJECTAGG(k VALUE v ABSENT ON NULL), over table rows where some rows have both k and v NULL. Today those rows are skipped and the query returns an object. After a minor release that carries this fix, the whole query fails with "field name must not be null", and the user finds out in production.
refuted.argument: [P11] was withdrawn because stricter validation of input that has no effect on the result made the command "unnecessarily less flexible". Message #6 makes the same point here: one can argue that keys need no check when the pair is skipped, and that only the documentation wording requires it. No reply in the thread defends the stricter reading on its merits, and nobody has checked the SQL standard. [P7] shows that a behavior change in SQL/JSON, even one the standard requires, was reverted until it was made deliberately and documented on its own.
refuted.author_must_show: Does the SQL standard require validating keys of pairs that ABSENT ON NULL omits, and will this change go to master only, with a release note?

precedents.title: COPY: validate option presence rather than option values
Revert cascading of JSON_TABLE's ON ERROR

critic.reasoning: Message #6 shows jsonb_object_agg_strict(NULL, NULL) already fails with "field name must not be null", so the scenario is today's behavior. The back-patch concern is a duplicate of standards-compat-1, and [P11] concerns COPY options.

refuted.title: Rejecting NULL keys paired with NULL values can break existing aggregate queries
refuted.failure_scenario: A report runs JSON_OBJECTAGG(k VALUE v ABSENT ON NULL RETURNING json) over a LEFT JOIN, so unmatched rows give NULL for both k and v. Today those rows are skipped and the query returns an object. After a minor-release update with this patch, the same query fails with a NULL-key error, and the user finds out in production.
refuted.argument: The brief says the json path now accepts NULL keys whenever the value is NULL, and v2 extends the change to JSON_OBJECTAGG and json_object_agg_strict() (message #7). An outer join that produces NULL for both key and value is a common pattern, so some users likely depend on the current result. Dolgov noted that skipping validation for omitted pairs is a defensible reading (message #6), and nobody replied to that point. The thread does not say whether this is master-only or will be back-patched, and it does not plan a release note.
refuted.author_must_show: Is this change limited to master with a release-note entry, and what is the reason to reject an all-NULL pair instead of keeping today's result?

precedents.title: COPY: validate option presence rather than option values

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. Its left join scenario also describes current behavior, because the aggregate transition functions check for a NULL key before the ABSENT ON NULL skip.

refuted.title: Stricter key checks may break working LEFT JOIN aggregates with no user gain
refuted.failure_scenario: A user runs JSON_OBJECTAGG(k VALUE v ABSENT ON NULL) or json_object_agg_strict(k, v) over a LEFT JOIN, so unmatched rows give a NULL key with a NULL value. Today the query returns an object without those rows. After the upgrade it raises an error, and the user finds out in production, possibly in a minor release.
refuted.argument: The only demand in the thread is one bug report, and it is a reading of the documentation (message #1). It shows no wrong result, no data loss and no user harm. Dmitry Dolgov noted that skipping validation for omitted pairs is a defensible reading (message #6), and no one has answered that point on its merits. Users who rely on today's lenient behavior pay the cost, while the gain is consistency with documentation that v2 rewrites to match the new behavior.
refuted.author_must_show: Is there a user for whom the current {} result caused a wrong answer, and will the change be master-only with a release-note entry?

critic.reasoning: The aggregates already reject a NULL key paired with a NULL value (message #6 shows the jsonb case), so the left join scenario is not a new failure. The remaining cost and design points duplicate standards-compat-1 and standards-compat-2.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: v2 adds a shared helper json_validate_key_category() used by json.c and jsonb.c.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The patch changes which keys JSON_OBJECT and JSON_OBJECTAGG accept under ABSENT ON NULL, with no check against the SQL standard.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: A dumped view, check constraint or generated column whose expression hits a newly rejected key can fail when restored or refreshed.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: It is tagged as a bug fix, and queries that return {} today would raise an error if it reaches stable branches.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The documentation now promises key validation for omitted pairs, which future constructor changes must keep.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The patch adds a key type classification for each pair that ABSENT ON NULL omits.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Is the fix meant for master only, or also for stable branches where queries that return {} today would start to fail?
What does the SQL standard say about a NULL key whose pair ABSENT ON NULL drops, and does the patch follow it?
Which release-note text tells users that ABSENT ON NULL now rejects NULL or non-scalar keys paired with NULL values?
What is the reason to validate keys of omitted pairs, given the point in message #6 that skipping the check is a defensible reading?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows the SQL/JSON constructors and the json and jsonb aggregate code would have to own it. The visible thread shows review comments but no statement from a committer on the behavior change.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a user-visible behavior change in JSON_OBJECT, JSON_OBJECTAGG and the two strict aggregates, and for the back-patch decision. The new documentation sentence makes the stricter rule a lasting promise.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 in response to review and v3 as a rebase, which is a sign of staying with the patch.

priority.reason: The patch is small and touches only json.c, jsonb.c, the sqljson tests and the documentation. It affects only queries that pair an invalid key with a NULL value under ABSENT ON NULL, and it needs a committer's decision on back-patching and the standard.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the claim that omitted keys never reach output or cast functions is unchecked. Only the v1 commit message and 3 of 8 messages were available, so the v2 helper and documentation text could not be judged.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add jsonb_translate(jsonb, from, to)
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andrew Dunstan, Pavel Stehule, Peter Eisentraut
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds jsonb_translate(jsonb, from, to), and in v2 json_translate, which recursively replaces every value, including array elements, that exactly equals a given string with another string. The author meant it for mapping categorical or enum values deep inside a document, in the style of the Unix tr utility.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andrew Dunstan judged blind replacement of every instance of a string, regardless of context, to be a niche use and asked why it could not be an extension. Pavel Stehule suggested using JsonPath to say what to replace, and Peter Eisentraut pointed to json_transform in Oracle and the SQL standard draft, noting that json_transform and json_translate together might confuse users. The thread ends there, and the author later withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Blindly replacing every
instance of a single string regardless of context seems at best a niche
use. Is there any reason not to make this an extension?

precedents_retrieved.title: Implement NULL-related checks in object address functions to prevent cache lookup errors
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set makes the SQL functions pg_describe_object, pg_identify_object and pg_identify_object_as_address return NULL for undefined objects instead of raising "cache lookup failed" errors. It adds missing_ok flags to getObjectDescription, getObjectIdentity and lower-level lookup routines such as get_attname, GetForeignServer and the publication and subscription lookups.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Several preparatory patches were committed during the thread, but the main objectaddress patch was not. In its last review, Alvaro Herrera found that pg_identify_object returned an empty type in only some cases, and that it reported a column for a relation with no such column. The author fixed the column case, but left open whether type, operator and function formatting should be reworked to return NULL for undefined objects. The visible messages show no reply after that, and no closing message.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: One thing is that I am not sure if it is worth complicating the existing interface even more just to deal with undefined objects as pure NULLs.

precedents_retrieved.title: make psql backslash commands honor "\pset null"
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes the special handling of NULL values in psql backslash commands, which set nullPrint = NULL in src/bin/psql/describe.c. Commands such as \dp would then honor "\pset null", so a NULL ACL (default privileges) can be told apart from an empty one.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch on the day he posted it, after he saw that a conflicting proposal existed and said he would reply on that thread. No one objected to the patch in the visible messages.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I just realize that there is a conflicting proposal.

precedents_retrieved.title: Jsonb transform for pl/python
precedents_retrieved.summary: A set of extensions (jsonb_plpythonu, jsonb_plpython2u, jsonb_plpython3u) implementing a CREATE TRANSFORM for jsonb in PL/Python, mapping jsonb objects to dicts, arrays to lists, and numerics to Python Decimal via string conversion, and back. The transform works in both directions so functions can take and return jsonb as native Python values.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The reviewer objected that the third version turned unsupported Python objects such as set() into JSON strings instead of raising an error, asked for tests and errors for complex numbers and ranges, and reported that the tests failed on Python 3. The author sent no revised version after that review, and the commitfest manager returned the patch with feedback because it still needed work and had had no updates for more than a week.

precedents_retrieved.title: Missing dependency on oauth_validator test
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the `oauth_hook_client` binary as a test dependency in the oauth_validator meson.build file, so the binary is built before the test runs. Without it, `meson test --suite oauth_validator` failed when the build did not enable the OAuth test through `PG_EXTRA_TEST`.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The only message is the author's proposal, and there are no replies.

precedents_retrieved.title: NOT VALID for Unique Indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary: Simon Riggs proposed allowing an existing index to be switched between unique and non-unique via ALTER INDEX SET [NOT] UNIQUE [NOT VALID] and ALTER INDEX VALIDATE UNIQUE, so uniqueness could be added without a long write-excluding scan and validated later in a separate transaction. The WIP patch added a new pg_index column (induniquevalid) and did not yet implement the index validation scan.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No deciding objection was raised; reviewers were positive and asked only design questions. The author said he could not finish the patch for the next commitfest and would complete it later, and a later message noted the patch no longer applied to HEAD and asked for an updated version, with no reply shown. The entry was left incomplete with no updated version posted.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I won't be able to finish this patch in time for this next CF, but
thanks for your interest, I will complete for PG15 later this year.

Avoid obscure DES key buffer loop bounds in pgcrypto

roaster_notes.note: No precedent proposes the same idea. The one objection rests on the behavior change and its unsettled back-patch scope.
Two objections, both about the user-facing contract. Design inside json.c and jsonb.c is outside this angle.

The proposal adds no WAL, catalog, protocol or ABI change. It changes only which key inputs JSON_OBJECT, JSON_OBJECTAGG and the *_agg_strict functions reject. An index, generated column or check constraint built on such an expression with an invalid key paired with NULL would now fail on REINDEX or new writes, but the material shows no user who has this, and the back-patch question belongs to another angle.

The patch only adds earlier type-category checks on keys in JSON constructors and the strict aggregates, so it has no privilege or exposure aspect. Per messages #2, #4 and #7 it calls no output or cast functions for omitted keys, so no user-defined code runs that did not run before.
From the maintenance angle the fix is small and contained. The shared helper Dolgov asked for reduces duplication, and the extra key classification runs only for omitted pairs.

This is a bug fix that makes key validation in JSON_OBJECT, JSON_OBJECTAGG and the *_object_agg_strict() functions consistent. No existing feature, extension or external tool can make core constructors reject these keys, so nothing from this angle applies. The patch reuses the existing category checks through one shared helper and adds no second mechanism. Back-patching and whether the change is desirable at all belong to other angles.
This is a consistency bug fix, and its demand is a single report. The one objection asks whether the stricter checks are worth breaking queries that work today.
